subject: Sequencing check: procurement & signoff cadence for Catalyst Health
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@catalysthealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-08T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement outline for Redwood pilot

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to share a short rundown of the approvals they need from our side so we can align sequencing (MSA / DPA / Order Form). High level:

- Legal needs a copy of Redwood's standard DPA and an explanation of data residency controls for our pilot environment.
- Procurement wants an orderform template and a confirmation of billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly).
- Budget owner needs a firm start / end for the 90-day pilot before PO issuance.

We have a target board approval window the week of Nov 27, which pushes signature expectations into early December if legal review is quick. If Redwood needs an MSA signature first, procurement would like to understand if an interim order form or PO can be issued to lock rates.

I attached the procurement checklist and the SOW draft that the budget owner will reference. Can you confirm the recommended sequencing from Redwood's perspective (we prefer MSA -> DPA -> Order Form but can be pragmatic if you have a staged sign-off approach)?

Claire
Claire Dawson
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Catalyst Health

Attachments: Catalyst_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), Catalyst_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement outline for Redwood pilot

Claire — really helpful summary, thanks. Quick notes from our side and a proposed lightweight sequencing to avoid blocking the pilot start:

1) Preferred sequence (low friction):
   - Sign MSA (governs commercial terms) with a negotiated appendix for pilot limits
   - Execute DPA (data procession terms) in parallel — we can provide our standard DPA and a one-page summary of residency controls for your legal to review first
   - Sign Order Form (captures SKU/prices) last; we can accept a PO to reserve capacity before final signed orderform if that helps procurement

2) If your board needs a start date before MSA signature: we can support a short-term SOW + PO that references the final MSA terms to follow (30-day bridge). That keeps the pilot timing intact.

3) Logistics / approvals:
   - Laura: can you confirm we can provide an abbreviated DPA summary for Claire to circulate to their counsel?
   - Karthik: request your input on accepting a PO vs. signed order form for pilot reservation.

If that aligns, we’ll draft a one-page sequencing timeline (MSA milestone dates + DPA review window + order form sign window) and send to Claire by EOD tomorrow.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@catalysthealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-10T08:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement outline for Redwood pilot

Markus / Laura,

Thanks — that sequencing sounds workable. Couple of constraints to flag from our side after a quick sync with counsel & procurement:

- Counsel prefers to review Redwood's full DPA before an MSA execution if data handling details materially differ from standard terms.
- Procurement will accept a PO to reserve pilot capacity but needs the orderform signed within 30 days of PO to finalize budget reconciliation.
- Our procurement lead will be on leave Nov 20–27; if we want an earlier board review, we need internal signoffs the week of Nov 13.

Attached is our procurement checklist (filled in) — you’ll see a few cells where counsel wants clarification on audit logs and subprocessor lists. If you can mark up the DPA or provide a short memo on audit/subprocessor practices, counsel may allow MSA-first execution.

I’m dropping the budget owner on copy. If Redwood can provide: 1) a 1-page DPA summary, 2) a timeline that shows a 2-week DPA review window and 30-day orderform sign window, we can align to either Nov 13 or Nov 27 board dates depending on internal approvals.

Claire

Attachments: Catalyst_Procurement_Checklist_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-10T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Sequencing check: procurement & signoff cadence for Catalyst Health

Team — forwarding Claire's note. Draft plan below that I’ll send to Claire if you both agree:

Draft sequencing timeline (proposed):
- Day 0 (Nov 13): Redwood sends MSA redline + standard DPA and 1-page DPA summary to Catalyst counsel
- Day 3–10 (Nov 16–23): Catalyst counsel reviews; Redwood stands by for three clarifying Qs (audit logs, subprocessors, residency controls)
- Day 11–14 (Nov 24–27): MSA sign window (conditional on minor redlines)
- Day 15–45 (Nov 28–Dec 28): Order Form sign window; Catalyst can issue PO on Day 15 to reserve capacity — PO must convert to signed Order Form within 30 days

Fallbacks / mitigations:
- If counsel wants full DPA review first, we will: provide the DPA + annotated notes and accept a PO + short SOW to begin pilot (30-day bridge).
- If orderform sign slips past Dec 28, we will hold quoted pricing for 10 business days after the PO expiry and then re-quote.

Ask: Laura — can you produce the 1-page DPA summary and the annotated DPA (highlighting our audit/subprocessor statements) by COB today? Karthik — confirm we can accept PO + SOW as bridge and whether finance needs any additional gating language.

If we get these two items today I’ll send the timeline to Claire and request Nov 13 as the optimistic path (to hit their earlier board window).

— Markus

On Nov 10, 2028, at 08:04 AM, Claire Dawson wrote:
> Markus / Laura,
> 
> Thanks — that sequencing sounds workable...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-12T09:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sequencing check: procurement & signoff cadence for Catalyst Health

Agree with the sequencing Markus outlined. A few operational clarifications from Sales Ops / Finance: 

1) PO as bridge: Finance will accept a PO to reserve capacity for up to 30 days provided the PO references a final-effective-date clause that points to the MSA signature date (or an agreed-upon fallback). We want a line that protects Redwood in case procurement cancels before execution.

2) Pricing hold: We can lock pricing for 10 business days after PO receipt. If Order Form not signed within that window, pricing may be reissued (we can offer a one-time extension for standard enterprise deals).

3) DPA summary & redline: Laura — happy to route the DPA summary to Finance counsel once you have it; we should avoid sending full annotated legal text to the customer — instead provide a 1-page summary + a clean DPA and offer to do a joint call with counsel if needed.

I'll draft a one-page sequencing timeline and template language for the PO-as-bridge clause and share by EOD. If we push for Nov 13 we need Laura's DPA summary today so I can include it in the timeline to Claire.

— Karthik
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
